fasti.note: Fravitta, a pagan Goth, had destroyed Gainas' fleet. Alaric invades Italy (November).
Battle of Pollentia (6 April, Easter) and Verona (summer 402 or 403): Stilicho checks Alaric. Court moves from Milan to Ravenna (by 402).
Theodosius II, aged one, consul for the first time.
Honorius' sixth consulship celebrated in Rome (Claudian's panegyric). Last recorded gladiatorial combat at Rome (Telemachus' martyrdom, Theodoret; date uncertain). John Chrysostom exiled.
Stilicho's second consulship was not recognised in the East, which dated by Anthemius alone. Radagaisus invades Italy (405-406); defeated at Faesulae (23 August 406).
Rhine crossing by Vandals, Alans and Sueves (31 December 406, or 405 on Kulikowski's argument). Usurpations in Britain: Marcus, Gratian.
Constantine III proclaimed in Britain and crosses to Gaul.

Arcadius dies (1 May); Theodosius II aged seven, under the prefect Anthemius. Stilicho executed at Ravenna (22 August); massacre of barbarian soldiers' families. Alaric's first siege of Rome; ransom of 5,000 pounds of gold and 30,000 of silver.

Constantine III recognised by Honorius as colleague and consul in his realm (Honorius VIII and Constantine). Alaric's second siege; Priscus Attalus proclaimed emperor by the Senate. Vandals, Alans and Sueves enter Spain (28 September or 13 October).

Tertullus was the consul of the usurper Attalus and recognised only in Rome; Honorius' court recognised Varanes. Sack of Rome by Alaric (24-27 August). Death of Alaric in Bruttium. 'Rescript of Honorius' to Britain (Zosimus 6.10), possibly to Bruttium.
The West named no consul and used post-consular dating. Constantius (III) defeats Constantine III at Arles; Jovinus proclaimed in Gaul. Conference of Carthage against the Donatists.
Athaulf leads the Goths into Gaul.
Heraclianus, comes Africae, revolted and invaded Italy; defeated, executed and his consulship annulled. The East dated by Lucius. Augustine begins the City of God (413-426).
Athaulf marries Galla Placidia at Narbo (January 414). Attalus again proclaimed by the Goths.
Hypatia murdered at Alexandria (March 415). Athaulf murdered at Barcelona; Wallia succeeds.
Treaty of Constantius with Wallia: Placidia returned for 600,000 measures of grain; Goths fight Vandals and Alans in Spain.
Constantius marries Galla Placidia (1 January). Rutilius Namatianus' De reditu suo (417).
Visigoths settled in Aquitania Secunda with Toulouse as base. Council of the Seven Provinces at Arles revived.
Both eastern nominees, recognised in the West.
Roman-Persian war (420-422).
Constantius made Augustus (8 February) but not recognised by Constantinople; dies 2 September. Theodosius II marries Eudocia (Athenais).
Peace with Persia; freedom of worship for Christians in Persia and Zoroastrians in Rome. Payments to the Huns begin (350 pounds of gold, rising later).
Honorius dies at Ravenna (15 August); the primicerius notariorum John usurps in the West.
Castinus was named by the usurper John and not recognised by the East or later. Eastern expedition under Ardabur and Aspar against John.

John captured at Ravenna and executed at Aquileia. Valentinian III (aged six) made Augustus at Rome (23 October); Placidia regent. Aetius brings 60,000 Huns (Philostorgius) too late, bought off. University of Constantinople (the 'Capitol') founded (27 February 425).
Law of Citations names Papinian, Paul, Ulpian, Modestinus and Gaius as authorities (CTh 1.4.3, 7 November 426).
Revolt of Boniface in Africa; expedition against him.
Nestorius bishop of Constantinople. Gaiseric becomes king of the Vandals.
Vandals cross to Africa (May); 80,000 by Victor of Vita's count. Commission for the Theodosian Code (renewed 435).
Augustine dies during the Vandal siege of Hippo (28 August). Aetius kills the magister militum Felix.
Council of Ephesus (Theotokos); Nestorius deposed. Whether this Bassus is the consul of 408 iterating or a namesake is disputed.
Boniface defeats Aetius near Ariminum, dies of wounds; Aetius flees to the Huns. Patrick's mission to Ireland (traditional date).
Aetius returns with Hunnic support and becomes magister utriusque militiae and patrician (433-435).
Attila and Bleda succeed Ruga (c. 434-435).
Treaty of Hippo (11 February) settles the Vandals in Numidia and Mauretania. Treaty of Margus doubles Hun tribute to 700 pounds.
Both apparently eastern nominees. Aetius' Hunnic auxiliaries destroy the Burgundian kingdom at Worms (436-437), the basis of the Nibelung legend.
Both western nominees. Valentinian III marries Licinia Eudoxia at Constantinople (29 October).
Theodosian Code promulgated (15 February), in force from 1 January 439; presented to the Senate in Rome (gesta senatus, 25 December 438).
Gaiseric takes Carthage (19 October), ending the 435 treaty.
Vandals raid Sicily. Leo I bishop of Rome.
Cyrus of Panopolis, the poet-prefect who rebuilt the walls and lit Constantinople at night; the West named no consul. Huns attack the Danube cities (Viminacium, Margus, Naissus).
Treaty with Gaiseric recognises Vandal control of the richest African provinces (Byzacena, Proconsularis, eastern Numidia).
Paterius' origin is uncertain. Burgundians resettled in Sapaudia. Anatolius' treaty with Attila: arrears of 6,000 pounds and 2,100 per year.
Valentinian III's novel against Pelagians and Manichaeans; western fiscal crisis (Nov. Val. 15 on the siliquaticum, 444/445).
Attila murders Bleda (c. 445).
Both apparently western nominees. The appeal of the Britons 'to Aetius, thrice consul' (Gildas, De excidio 20) is dated 446-454 by the title.
Earthquake throws down the Theodosian walls (26 January); rebuilt in 60 days. Attila's great Balkan campaign; battle of the Utus. Ardabur is the son of Aspar.
Priscus' embassy to Attila (449). Bacaudae in Gaul under Eudoxius.
'Robber Council' (Latrocinium) of Ephesus (August).
Both western nominees. Theodosius II dies after a riding fall (28 July); Pulcheria marries Marcian, who stops tribute to Attila. Honoria's ring offered to Attila. Galla Placidia dies (27 November).

Attila invades Gaul; besieges Orléans; defeated by Aetius and Theodoric I at the Catalaunian Plains (20 June?), where Theodoric I is killed. Council of Chalcedon (October): Christ in two natures; canon 28 on Constantinople's rank.
Attila invades Italy; Aquileia destroyed; turns back after the embassy of Pope Leo, Avienus and Trygetius (and plague and an eastern attack on his homeland).
Attila dies on his wedding night (453); Hunnic empire breaks up after Nedao (454).
Both eastern. The eastern Aetius is a different man. Valentinian III personally murders Aetius on the Palatine at Ravenna (21 or 22 September).

Valentinian III assassinated by Aetius' bucellarii (16 March). Petronius Maximus emperor; killed fleeing (31 May). Vandal sack of Rome (2-16 June); Eudoxia and her daughters taken to Carthage. Avitus proclaimed at Arles (9 July) with Visigothic backing.

Avitus' consulship was not recognised in the East, which named Iohannes and Varanes. Sidonius' panegyric on Avitus (1 January). Ricimer defeats a Vandal fleet off Corsica and deposes Avitus at Placentia (October). Theodoric II defeats the Sueves at the Órbigo.

Both eastern consuls; the West recognised them. Marcian dies (27 January); Leo I proclaimed (7 February) with Aspar's backing, crowned by the patriarch (debated). Majorian proclaimed (1 April or 28 December 457).
Majorian's legislation (Novels) on tax arrears, curiales, defensores, and monuments of Rome.
Majorian recovers Gaul from Theodoric II.
Majorian's invasion fleet of 300 ships destroyed by the Vandals at Portus Ilicitanus (Cartagena area).
Majorian deposed by Ricimer at Dertona (2 August) and executed (7 August). Libius Severus proclaimed (19 November), not recognised by Leo.
Severus' consulship not recognised in the East. Aegidius' breakaway command in northern Gaul (domain of Soissons). Marcellinus in Dalmatia independent.
Battle of Orléans: Aegidius defeats the Visigoths.
Olybrius, later emperor (472), consul in the East. Aegidius dies; Paul and then Syagrius in Soissons.
Both eastern; Hermenericus was a son of Aspar. Libius Severus dies (14 November); interregnum in the West (465-467). Great fire of Constantinople.
Leo III sole consul; any western nomination in the interregnum is not securely attested. Euric murders his brother Theodoric II and becomes Visigothic king.
No western consul. Anthemius proclaimed in the West (12 April) with eastern backing; his daughter marries Ricimer.

Anthemius sole consul (as Augustus, recognised by both courts). The joint East-West expedition against the Vandals under Basiliscus (over 1,000 ships, 64,000 or 120,000 pounds of gold) destroyed by fireships off Cape Bon.
Marcian is Anthemius' son. Arvandus, praetorian prefect of Gaul, tried for treason (letter to Euric).
Euric expands the Visigothic kingdom; Riothamus' Britons defeated at Bourg-de-Déols (469/470).
Aspar and his son Ardabur murdered in the palace at Constantinople. Theodoric (the Amal) begins his career on his return as a hostage.
Ricimer besieges Rome and kills Anthemius (11 July); Olybrius emperor; Ricimer dies (18 August); Olybrius dies (October or November). Gundobad the kingmaker.
West without consuls: Glycerius proclaimed (3 or 5 March) by Gundobad, not recognised by Leo.
Leo II, the infant grandson of Leo I, sole consul. Leo I dies (18 January); Leo II and his father Zeno co-emperors; Leo II dies (November). Julius Nepos deposes Glycerius (June).

Basiliscus seizes Constantinople (January); Zeno flees to Isauria. Orestes expels Nepos from Ravenna and makes his son Romulus Augustus emperor (31 October). Euric gains Auvergne by treaty with Nepos.

Odoacer proclaimed king by the federate troops (23 August); Orestes killed at Placentia (28 August); Romulus Augustulus deposed and pensioned in Campania (4 September); imperial regalia sent to Constantinople. Zeno restored (August). The West named no consuls this year.
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Basilisci II et Armati) in both halves. Gaiseric dies (25 January).
Illus, the Isaurian general, consul in the East and recognised in Italy.
Zeno sole consul. Revolt of Marcian (son of Anthemius) at Constantinople suppressed.
Odoacer resumes western nominations. Julius Nepos murdered in Dalmatia (9 May); Odoacer annexes Dalmatia (481).
Clovis succeeds Childeric I (481 or 482).
Zeno's Henotikon (482) seeks to reconcile Chalcedonians and Miaphysites; leads to the Acacian schism (484-519) with Rome.
The East named no consul (or it was not recognised in Italy).
Theodoric the Amal consul in the East. Revolt of Illus and Leontius (484-488). Huneric's persecution of Nicene Christians in Africa (conference of Carthage, 1 February 484).
Symmachus, later Boethius' father-in-law.
Clovis defeats Syagrius at Soissons, ending the Roman enclave in northern Gaul.
Father of the philosopher Boethius.
Both consuls named in the West. Zeno commissions Theodoric to invade Italy against Odoacer.
Theodoric defeats Odoacer on the Isonzo (28 August) and at Verona (30 September).
Battle of the Adda (11 August); Odoacer besieged in Ravenna (490-493).
Zeno dies (9 April); Anastasius chosen by the empress Ariadne, who marries him. Isaurian War (492-497).
Both eastern.
Odoacer surrenders Ravenna (5 March) and is killed by Theodoric at a banquet (15 March).
Praesidius' origin is uncertain. Asterius' colophon on the Medicean Virgil records his edition during his consulship.
Clovis defeats the Alamanni (Tolbiac); baptism of Clovis (496, 498 or 508 debated).
Anastasius recognises Theodoric's rule in Italy and returns the palace regalia.
Anastasius abolishes the chrysargyron (collatio lustralis) and introduces the follis coinage reform (498).
Theodoric's visit to Rome (tricennalia); grain distributions and wall repairs.
Laurentian schism at Rome (498-506).
Avienus iunior, son of Faustus Niger, not the consul of 501. Kavadh I invades Roman Mesopotamia; Theodosiopolis (Erzurum) and Amida (January 503) fall.
Anastasian Persian War (502-506).
Amida recovered by purchase (504/505). Theodoric's forces take Sirmium (504).
Dara (Anastasiopolis) fortified on the frontier (505-507).
Breviary of Alaric (Lex Romana Visigothorum) issued (2 February 506).
Clovis defeats and kills Alaric II at Vouillé; the Visigoths lose most of Gaul.
Clovis receives an honorary consulship (codicils) from Anastasius at Tours (Gregory of Tours 2.38). Ostrogoths secure Provence.
Boethius, philosopher, sole consul.
Death of Clovis (27 November); Council of Orléans.
Riots at Constantinople over the Trisagion addition; Anastasius offers to abdicate in the Hippodrome.
Revolt of Vitalian in Thrace (513-515). Clementinus' consular diptych survives (Liverpool).
Cassiodorus, author of the Variae and the Chronica (which ends at 519).
Vitalian's fleet burned by Marinus (with 'sulphur', per Malalas).
The eastern Anastasius was the emperor's grandnephew. Burgundian Council of Epaone.
Anastasius dies (9 July); Justin I, commander of the excubitors, chosen.
Eutharic, Theodoric's son-in-law and designated heir, consul with the emperor as his colleague. End of the Acacian schism (28 March).
Vitalian murdered in the palace (July).
Justinian's consulship games cost 288,000 solidi (Marcellinus comes).
The two sons of Boethius, both named in the West and accepted by Justin as a sign of goodwill; Boethius magister officiorum.
Boethius arrested on a charge of treasonable correspondence with Constantinople; Consolation of Philosophy written in prison.
Boethius executed (524 or 526).
Pope John I sent to Constantinople by Theodoric. Dionysius Exiguus' Easter tables introduce AD dating (525).
Theodoric dies (30 August); Amalasuntha regent for Athalaric. Earthquake destroys Antioch (May 526): 250,000 dead per Malalas.
Justinian co-emperor (1 April); Justin dies (1 August).
Commission for the Codex Justinianus (13 February). Earthquake at Antioch.
First Codex Justinianus (7 April). Academy at Athens loses its funding (529). Samaritan revolt. Benedict at Monte Cassino (traditional).
Both western. Battle of Dara: Belisarius defeats the Persians.
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Lampadii et Orestis). Battle of Callinicum (Easter). Khosrow I succeeds Kavadh (September).

No consuls: second year after the consulship of Lampadius and Orestes. Nika riot (13-18 January): 30,000 killed in the Hippodrome; Hagia Sophia burned. 'Eternal Peace' with Persia (11,000 pounds of gold).
Digest (16 December) and Institutes (21 November) promulgated. Belisarius conquers the Vandal kingdom: Ad Decimum (13 September), Tricamarum (December).

Decius Paulinus the last western (Italian) consul. Second Codex Justinianus (16 November). Gelimer surrenders; Belisarius' triumph at Constantinople. Athalaric dies; Amalasuntha shares power with Theodahad.
Belisarius consul (sole). Amalasuntha murdered (30 April); Gothic War begins; Belisarius takes Sicily. Volcanic dust veil ('dimmed sun') of 535/536 (Procopius, Cassiodorus).
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Belisarii). Belisarius takes Naples and enters Rome (9/10 December); Witigis king of the Goths.

No consuls: second year after Belisarius. Witigis besieges Rome (March 537-March 538). Hagia Sophia dedicated (27 December). Justinian's Novel 47 (31 August 537) requires documents to be dated by the regnal year first.
Iohannes the Cappadocian, praetorian prefect, consul.
Apion of the Egyptian landowning family. Franks under Theudebert invade Italy.
Iustinus, son of Germanus. Belisarius takes Ravenna (May); Witigis to Constantinople. Khosrow I sacks Antioch and deports its people to 'Weh Antiok Khosrow'.

Basilius, a Roman aristocrat nominated in the East, was the last ordinary consul; afterwards years were reckoned post consulatum Basilii (counting to p.c. XXV in 566), until Justin II revived the title as part of the imperial office (566). Totila king of the Goths. Plague of Justinian reaches Pelusium (July 541) and Constantinople (spring 542).
